description: Logging off, the investigators rest and recuperate, discussing strategies for entering through the side door and avoiding direct confrontation.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Qiduo received! Continuing to record the horror of the Orient Express for you. Currently, 7126 texts have been recorded, taking 35 hours, 25 minutes, and 2 seconds. Huh? A piece of paper flew out when opening the file. No matter how capable a person is, they ultimately cannot defy fate.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: So, as we left off last time, player4 finished skinning and returned to the hotel with their companions. What will you all do now?

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: "So, are there any other materials to prepare? player4, I can lend a hand." #Swallows saliva, looking at the backpack containing human skin. The faint smell of blood makes Johnson feel slightly uneasy.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Check the time.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Midnight, 12 o'clock.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "How about sleeping first? It's a bit late."

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: "Then I'll set up the magic circle and such first, and you guys can continue tomorrow? I keep late hours, you guys sleep first."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Yawns.

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: #Takes down the bag containing human skin and fiddles with it. #Can't figure it out, gives up in frustration and goes to sleep. #ZZZ

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Here it comes.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: On the morning of January 15th, a copy of the Milan Morning Post slid in through the newspaper slot in the door. The front-page headline featured news of Mussolini inspecting a newly built automobile factory, with a picture of the leader patting the hood of a brand-new Alfa Romeo sports car. Turning to the second page, three news items side by side caught the eye: Opera Star Missing! Feared Kidnapped. Police fear soprano singer Caterina Cavallaro may have been kidnapped from Milan's Central Station. She hasn't been seen since getting off the train from Paris yesterday at 1 PM. Since then, she has neither returned to her apartment nor attended rehearsals at La Scala, where she is scheduled to perform Aida tomorrow night. Arturo Toscanini, the music director of La Scala, stated he hasn't heard from Cavallaro since she left Paris. Police ask anyone with information about Caterina's whereabouts to contact them. We sincerely urge all Milanese to join the search for our beloved star. Auto Worker Murdered. The body of auto worker Neo Spinola was found this morning in an alley on Via Tavazzano in the Portello district, not far from the Alfa Romeo factory where he worked. Spinola was stabbed to death. Police are investigating workers in the area. Spinola was an active union member and reportedly had arguments with other workers about union matters a few days ago. Popular Return. At last night's banquet for La Scala's patrons and supporters, Flavio Conti was warmly welcomed. Mr. Conti has been unwell in recent months, with some erroneous reports claiming he had tuberculosis, but clearly the situation is not as serious as these fallacies suggested. Mr. Conti has fully recovered and was the center of attention at the banquet. Also in attendance were other opera patrons: Mr. Nuzio Tocci, Mr. Matteo Sorrenti and his wife, Ms. Angela Susco, Mr. Arturo Faccià, and Mrs. Serena Spagnolo. They enjoyed excerpts from the opera Aida, scheduled for this week, performed by the cast. Rosario Sobrero provided piano accompaniment, the highlight of the gathering. The entertainment section reminded in bold: Aida Premiere Countdown! Tomorrow night at 8 PM, La Scala Opera House, don't miss it. The social news column reported on Fascist youth groups burning decadent art books on Via Dante, with a picture showing several Freud works curling in flames. The classified ads were still filled with castor oil advertisements, but today's special recommendation was a new Swiss medicine specifically for lung ailments.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Scratches head while looking at the newspaper. "Do you guys have any leads?" #Asks other companions.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "No."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "I don't either." "How about we perform the ritual first?" .st san-1d4

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: <player4>'s "Sanity" change: 70 ➯ 68 (deduct -1d4=-2)

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: .ra Occult

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Belief arises from desire; if it's what you hope for, it will surely receive a response. <player4>'s Occult prayer: D100=86/50 Failure. -Life is good precisely because it's meaningless, allowing each to bestow their own meaning.

conversation.text: .st show Occult

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: <player5>'s currently registered personal information is as follows: Occult: 5. -Going to unleash a special move!

conversation.text: .st show Occult

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: <player12>'s currently registered personal information is as follows: Occult: 5. -Going to unleash a special move!

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: player4 suddenly feels a strong dizziness, almost dropping the ritual materials in hand. He sees a blood-red, unfamiliar room in the ritual bowl, filled with twisted medical instruments. His temples throb, and he hears the sound of incessant coughing echoing in his ears, as if countless tuberculosis patients are gasping around him. With a soft *snap*, the illusion suddenly shatters. player4 then realizes he has stumbled and bumped into the wardrobe, feeling real pain in his knee.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: .st san -1d4

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: <player4>'s "Sanity" change: 68 ➯ 65 (deduct -1d4=-3)

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: .ra Occult

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Belief arises from desire; if it's what you hope for, it will surely receive a response. <player4>'s Occult prayer: D100=59/50 Failure. -Well.. just missed by a bit.

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: "Ouch, take it easy player4, it's okay if the ritual didn't succeed." #Helps him up the wardrobe he bumped into.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Are you alright? ...Well, there's always a certain cost to dealing with this kind of thing."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: (You continue.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "It's a bit tricky, everyone." #Wipes sweat from forehead.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: player4 endured the headache and cast the spell again. As the incantation began, his vision suddenly went dark——

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Belief arises from desire; what you wish for will surely receive a response, <player4>'s willpower prayer:

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Although terrified, driven by intense curiosity, I decide to lean in and look!

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Inside the cabinet stood a stark white headless bust statue, its smooth torso gleaming with a bone-like cold light under the moonlight. The moment he clearly saw the statue, the thing suddenly toppled forward, with a speed that seemed unnatural for gravity!

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Oh shit!"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Thud!

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Cough cough cough"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #Recall the state of my companion earlier, compare it; the difference between when my companion fell into a trance and those similarly bizarre people outside.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "A white statue!"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The state player4 was in when he fell into the illusion was strikingly similar to the zombie-like citizens on the streets of Milan: equally vacant eyes, stiff bodies, slow response to external stimuli. The only difference was that player4 still trembled with fear, while those Milanese had even lost that instinct, as if their souls had been put on pause.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Recall if the statue I saw in the hallucination resembles the fragments we've collected.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "And based on your condition, we have reason to suspect."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Me earlier? I also turned into one of those living dead?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "There's an even bolder speculation..."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: A sharp, piercing pain suddenly shot through Bailan's left shoulder, as if an ice pick were chiseling into the bone marrow along an old wound.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Hiss..."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Bailan pulled open her collar, her pupils suddenly contracting. Strange dark red patterns had surfaced on the skin of her left arm, identical to the patterns on the left arm statue found earlier in Paris. The lines were slightly raised like blood vessels, pulsing faintly bright and dark with her breathing rhythm.

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: "Holy crap!" #Exclaimed, covering my mouth.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Move closer to carefully observe these patterns.

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: "Should we do something about it? It looks pretty scary."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: When player4 touched the patterns with his finger, he found the skin around them was cold as marble, completely unlike the body temperature of a living person.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: .ra occult

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Belief arises from desire; what you wish for will surely receive a response, <player4>'s occult prayer:

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: [Spell]

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: player4 stared at the patterns on Bailan's left shoulder and suddenly felt a strong sense of déjà vu. He had read similar records in the Devil's Simulacrum: The statue's owner shall bear the curse of the incomplete statue... In a flash of insight, he pieced together the curse's effects: left arm pain like a fracture, wrist spraining inexplicably, skin breaking out in eczema-like red rashes. The most terrifying is the late-stage symptom—the arm would uncontrollably repeat a certain motion, like the Milanese sleepwalkers, until the muscles become paralyzed and atrophy. It's in the early stages now. If we don't gather the statue quickly...

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: "Then... there's no time to lose. Let's act quickly."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Right. I think we should go check the theater."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: You find the business card the agent gave you yesterday, neatly printed with Giuseppe Totti - Bologna Music Agency. Below the contact information is a line of small text: Specializing in opera and solo performances.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Good idea"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Try contacting the agent, bluffing that there might be some leads on the big star's disappearance

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: After player4 dials the phone, the agent answers with a tired but alert voice: Rossi Agency, who is this?

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Yes, yes, we suspect there might be discoveries on the opera house stage"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Having an informant is great, slacking off, slacking off

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "If it's convenient for you, could you take us there? After all, we're unfamiliar faces, it might be inconvenient for us to handle things"

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: "Alright, we won't make a fuss, let's get to work first!"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #Not too much panic

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The agent immediately responds: The opera house? Good lord... you think she's there? Urgent rustling sounds come from the other end of the phone, I can come right now, wait for me at the café in the Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II—the one right across from the main entrance of La Scala.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Yes, yes, good, we'll wait for you there"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Oh, where were we? I was just thinking, could it be a group of terrorists already influenced by the statue who planned this case"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Hangs up the phone, relays the meeting address to everyone

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Passes are no problem, I have a few spare ones in my drawer. The crisp sound of keys jingling comes through the background, see you in twenty minutes... oh, don't wear anything too conspicuous, there have been black shirts hanging around near the opera house lately. They've been frequently monitoring cultural venues recently, um... in the name of maintaining the purity of traditional culture."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "The waters run deep here, it seems we're not the only ones looking for this statue"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Change into slightly plainer clothes

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #Change into a relatively plain outfit, ready to slip over and check the situation.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Change clothes, head to the meeting café according to the directions on the way

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Let's go, let's go, Johnson doesn't need to change, he's already plain enough

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: In the café of the Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II, crystal chandeliers make the gilded decorations shine brightly. Agent Rossi is ten minutes late, Sorry, got stopped by patrols twice on the way. He sits down breathlessly, pulls a few passes bearing the La Scala Opera House emblem from his briefcase, Now they search everyone going in and out... saying they're looking for some smuggled artifacts. His gold-rimmed glasses are fogged, but can't hide the dark circles under his eyes.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Accepts the passes

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: May the Madonna protect you, he knocks over the salt shaker when getting up but doesn't notice, I... I need to go to the police station to ask about the situation again. His back disappears into the crowd in the gallery.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #Glances at those people outside the window while looking down

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Those Blackshirt members look perfectly normal—they lounge lazily against the opera house columns smoking, one is teasing a stray cat with his boot tip, another is flipping through the day's newspaper. When passersby occasionally go by, they just give a routine glance, not even checking IDs.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Lowers voice "Let's go, let's check out the theater"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Passing under the magnificent glass dome of the Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II, the investigators arrive at Piazza della Scala. In the center of the square stands Michelangelo's statue, the bronze figure of this Renaissance master leans slightly forward, his chisel forever suspended in the air, as if about to give life to stone the next second. Scattered around the statue's base are a few bouquets of long-withered flowers—perhaps left from some memorial event. Directly opposite is the famous La Scala Opera House, its Neoclassical exterior unadorned. The light brown outer walls have no lavish decorations, only orderly rows of arched windows and the reliefs on the pediment reveal its identity.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Quite a low-key building"

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: "Yes, yes" #Echoes in agreement

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #Casually observes the statue, seems due to some reasons, has now developed a conditioned reflex risk when seeing statues.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Signed by Toscanini? The guard eyes them suspiciously The old man's in a worse mood than usual today... The props room is in the northwest corner, don't go near the patrons' boxes on the east side. Then he steps aside.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Are there any new props in the troupe recently? Especially for the new play performance, Aida."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Follow player4 inside

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #Prepare to follow forward after the questioning is done

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Find the Aida prop room as guided

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The guard frowned and flipped through the register: New props? Last week, a few crates of Egyptian-style shields and headdresses were delivered, all piled up in the corridor of the prop room.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Things having come to this, head to the prop room

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The investigators passed through a narrow passage into the backstage and were immediately surrounded by a chaotic scene. To the right, a wooden nose nearly three meters tall leaned against the wall—likely a prop for some comedic opera, with the word Pinocchio written in red paint on its tip. An actor playing the Pharaoh sat in the nose's shadow, his heavy golden crown askew, a cigar in one hand while he flung out a Spade Ace with the other; across the card table was an extra dressed in Nubian slave costume. On the floor, a dark red fake bloodstain snaked out from under the prop room door, tracing an eerie path across the cluttered ground. Several prop masters were stepping over the bloodstain, carrying fragments of Amun Temple columns back and forth, completely unconcerned about the increasingly smeared red marks underfoot. The air was filled with a cacophony of sounds: a soprano repeatedly practicing the same high note next door, the stage manager's whistle, the crisp hammering of a carpenter—everyone was working frantically as the performance time approached.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #After hearing these words, first look at the corridor situation, prioritize checking those newly arrived crates of shields and headdresses

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Professor Bailan cautiously looked around and soon spotted Toscanini's figure behind the glass window of the second-floor rehearsal hall. The irritable music director was waving his baton, scolding the choir as if herding sheep: You sing so badly even the crocodiles of the Nile would cover their ears!

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Examine if the current setup resembles the hallucination

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: "It can be described as chaotic" #Looking around
